theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners screen as the cleanest trend-following candidate among non-crowded, eligible themes: genuine trend hurst tag, the highest durability bar in the top ranks (0.73), and excellent breadth (0.92). Momentum score is mid-pack but positive and rising, while crowding is near zero (z=0.19), meaning the absolute-trend gate is doing the work without the reflexive over-extension risk that plagues the leader. The trend-gate leg is the only validated edge on this market, and GDX hits it without a crowding caution.
evidence: hurst_tag == 'trend' (only top-5 theme with this tag among scorable, non-crowded names)
breadth 0.917 — broad participation, not a narrow squeeze
crowding_z 0.19 — not crowded; no size-down caution triggered
eligible == true — inside the absolute-trend gate
theses.dissent: Gold miners are highly sensitive to real yields and the US dollar; an unscheduled macro surprise (geopolitics dominates the narrative flow at 98% unscheduled share) that strengthens the dollar or lifts real rates could hit GDX hard regardless of trend health. The detector has no forward return edge, so 'trend' only argues for staying power, not upside.

theses.subject: Silver Miners
theses.thesis: Silver Miners sit second in momentum with positive breadth (0.75) and a mixed-but-respectable durability bar (0.63), not crowded (z=0.52). It is the closest thing to a confirmed secondary leadership theme alongside gold, and the two miners names together suggest a precious-metals pulse rather than a single-name anomaly. Eligible under the trend gate. Lean is low-conviction because hurst is 'mixed' (not clean trend) and the momentum gap to the leader is wide (1.978 margin).
evidence: rank 2 with score 1.847 — clear second-place momentum
theses.dissent: Silver miners have higher beta than gold miners and a 'mixed' hurst tag — the trend is less established. If the industrial demand story (part of silver) weakens while the precious-metals bid stays gold-specific, SIL could underperform GDX meaningfully.

falsifier.text: SIL lags GDX by 4% or more over any 10-day stretch before the check-by date

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: The leader is crowded (z=1.42, flagged crowded) with a mean-revert hurst tag, zero breadth, and a low durability bar (0.43) relative to its outsized momentum score. The guardrails explicitly forbid fading the dominant theme on a crowding flag, so 'avoid' (do not add, size down via the crowding caution) is the correct expression — not a short. Reflexivity means the leader can persist, but the texture (isolated, mean-reverting, crowded) argues against new exposure here absent a confirmed acceleration in breadth.
evidence: hurst_tag 'mean-revert' — not a durable trend structure
crowding_z 1.42 + crowded == true — size-down caution triggered
breadth 0.0 — leadership is isolated, no participation
durability_bar 0.43 — low staying-power relative to score
theses.dissent: Reflexivity is real: the leading theme can stay crowded and keep rising much longer than trend-health metrics suggest, especially with AI/tech as a top macro narrative theme. Avoiding it is a missed-upside stance, not a shake-out call — and fading it would be worse.

falsifier.text: Memory/HBM (SMH proxy) closes at a new 20-day high with breadth rising above 0.2 before the check-by date
